ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-119, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale, reciting the fact of the General Municipal Election held on November 8, 2022,
declaring the result and such matters as provided by law.

RECOMMENDATION
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-119, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale, reciting the fact of the General Municipal Election held on November 8, 2022,
declaring the result and such matters as provided by law.

BACKGROUND
Resolution No. CC 2022-119 recites the fact of the General Municipal Election held on
November 8, 2022 for the purpose of electing three Councilmembers elected by
geographic Districts 3, 4, and 5 for four (4) year terms.

DISCUSSION
The California Elections Code states that the governing body of the City shall meet to
approve the canvass of the election and install the newly elected officers. The City Clerk
shall enter on the records of the City Council of the City, a statement of the results of
the election. Resolution No. CC 2022-119, and attached Exhibit A, the Certificate of the
Canvass of the Election Returns, are the statement of the results of the election.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with adopting Resolution No. CC 2022-119.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2022-122, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE MAKING
  LEGALLY REQUIRED FINDINGS AND EXTENDING REMOTE
  TELECONFERENCE PARTICIPATION FOR MEETINGS OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL AND/OR ITS RELATED OR
  SUBORDINATE LEGISLATIVE BODIES

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-122, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale authorizing remote teleconference participation for meetings of the City
Council and/or its subordinate legislative bodies for an additional 30-day period.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the resolution to thereby extend, for an additional 30-day period, the
  authority of the City Council, and all related and/or subordinate legislative bodies,
  to participate remotely in properly noticed meetings.

BACKGROUND
Since October 1, 2021 and through January 1, 2024, AB 361 has temporarily amended
the Ralph M. Brown Act (California Government Code § 54950 et seq.) to provide more
flexibility regarding participation in public meetings from a remote location. In layman’s
terms AB 361 allows “zoom” meetings if specified requirements are met.
If the City Council authorizes remote meetings, such initial authorization must expire no
later than 30 days from the initial authorization. The City Council is authorized to
thereafter extend the authorization if it makes one of various specified findings.
AB 361 requires several procedural safeguards to protect public participation during a
remote meeting, key ones of which are summarized as follows:
  1. The public must have the ability to address the legislative body directly and must
  be given information on how to address the legislative body;
  2. The public must be provided with either a call-in or internet-based service option;
  3. The legislative body must stop the meeting if the call-in or internet-based option
  fails;
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution No. CC 2022-122
December 21, 2022
Page 2

  4. The legislative body cannot require that public comments be submitted in
  advance (although this option can be provided);
  5. Public speakers cannot be required to pre-register for public comment (except as
  required by an independent call-in or internet platform);
  6. Members of the public must be given a reasonable time to register to provide
  public comment; and
  7. Agencies that provide a timed public comment period shall not close the public
  comment period until that time period has expired.
DISCUSSION
The City Council adopted an initial AB 361 Resolution on June 15, 2022. This resolution
has been extended multiple times. The most recent extension is set to expire on January
6, 2023. The question before the City Council is whether to extend this authority for an
additional 30-day period. An extension of authority to remotely participate is allowed if
(1) the state of emergency continues, and (2) a resolution with required findings has
been adopted within the last 30 days.
The proposed resolution would be immediately effective and allow members of
legislative bodies to continue to participate remotely for an additional thirty days if the
agenda for the meeting has included the legally required participation noticing. The
resolution would also allow the City Manager (or designee) to opt to not include such
noticing, as there may be instances where it would be impractical, due to staffing
considerations, to allow remote participation in meetings.
FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

SUBJECT:  AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY

  REGARDING THE SELECTION OF THE MAYOR AND MAYOR PRO
  TEM
ISSUE
Introduction and adoption of Ordinance No. U-1604, an Urgency Ordinance of the City
Council of the City, revising Municipal Code Section 2.08.010 regarding the selection of
the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. Also consider alternate versions of said ordinance, such
as a non-urgency ordinance.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Hold a public hearing to accept public testimony; and
  2. Consider whether to adopt Ordinance No. U-1604 on an urgency basis and/or
  whether to propose amendments to such proposed ordinance.

BACKGROUND
Until the November 2022 election, the position of mayor had been directly elected by the
electorate at large.
Palmdale Municipal Code 2.08.010 currently establishes that the for the one-year period
following the election, the person serving as Mayor is to be decided by lot (i.e., by random
selection), and then at the end of the first year, the position of mayor would rotate annually
when it provides:
  “Elected Mayor. The office of the Mayor of the City shall, beginning at the
  end of the elected Mayor’s term, be filled by one of the Councilmembers.
  The district from which the office of Mayor is initially filled shall be decided
  by lot as soon thereafter as reasonably practicable. Thereafter, the office of
  Mayor shall rotate every one year and will be decided by a majority of the
  City Council.”
The City Council has the option to amend the municipal code’s provisions regarding the
procedure to select the Mayor and/or the position of Mayor Pro Tem.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Urgency Ordinance No. 1602 – Mayoral and Mayor Pro Tem Selection
Page 2

The proposed ordinance would do the following:
    Annual Reorganization. Establish that each year, a majority of the City Council is
  to select who will serve as Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. In even-numbered years
  that decision is to occur immediately after the new City Council takes office (in the
  November/December time frame). In years when there are no City Council
  election results to be canvassed following a November election (typically, odd-
  numbered years), the City Council shall make such selections during the first
  regular City Council meeting of December. In years when there are election results
  to be canvassed following a November election (typically, even numbered years),
  the City Council shall make such selections at the same City Council meeting at
  which the City Council confirms the official canvass of the municipal election
  results consistent with Government Code 36801, and California Elections Code
  10261 and 10262. In other words, in most instances, the position of mayor would
  be voted on each December or thereabouts.
    Mayor / Mayor Pro Tem Qualifications. The ordinance would make clear that a
  person shall not become mayor or mayor pro tem if that person declines the
  position.
    Vacancies. If the position of Mayor is vacant, the Mayor Pro Tem would become
  the Mayor. If the position of Mayor Pro Tem is vacant, it would remain vacant until
  filled by the Council majority.
    Removal. Even though the City Council is required to yearly determine who is to
  be Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem, the City Council always retains the discretion to
  remove/replace the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem.
    Immediately Effective. The proposed ordinance is crafted as an urgency
  ordinance, and would become immediately effective if approved by no less than
  four members of the city council. If adopted, the City Council would select the
  Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem based upon the newly adopted ordinance. If only three
  members vote to approve the ordinance, then it could become effective as early
  as the 31st day after adoption. Upon it becoming effective, the Council majority
  could select a new Mayor and/or Mayor Pro Tem based upon the newly effective
  ordinance.

The proposed ordinance does not do any of the following:

SUBJECT:  SELECTION OF MAYOR

ISSUE
Selection of the Mayor.

RECOMMENDATION

urgency ordinance has been adopted which immediately amends the relevant
procedures, appoint a Mayor consistent with such new procedures.

BACKGROUND

the November 2022 election, the person serving as Mayor is to be decided by lot (i.e., by
random selection), and at the end of the first year, the position of mayor would rotate
annually:
  2.08.010. “Elected Mayor. The office of the Mayor of the City shall,
  beginning at the end of the elected Mayor’s term, be filled by one of the
  Councilmembers. The district from which the office of Mayor is initially filled
  shall be decided by lot as soon thereafter as reasonably practicable.
  Thereafter, the office of Mayor shall rotate every one year and will be
  decided by a majority of the City Council.”

then the selection of the Mayor is to occur “by lot” (i.e., at random). The City Clerk’s
department will have available at the meeting the materials available to randomly select
the first mayor.
If the City Council has adopted an urgency ordinance at the December 21 meeting, then
the City Council would select the Mayor pursuant to that new ordinance.

SUBJECT:  DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ACTION TO DECLARE A LOCAL
  EMERGENCY RELATED TO THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES’
  PROPOSED RELOCATION OF HOMELESS TO A “VILLAGE” IN
  PALMDALE

ISSUE
Discussion and possible action declaring a state of emergency related to the City of Los
Angeles’ proposed relocation of homeless individuals to Palmdale.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Discuss declaring a state of emergency;
  2. Take public comment;
  3. Declare a state of emergency related to the City of Los Angeles’ intent to relocate
  homeless populations to LA city or county owned land in Palmdale.

BACKGROUND
Karen Bass was elected to the office of Mayor of Los Angeles in November and sworn in
December 11, 2022. In her first act as mayor, she declared a state of emergency related
to homelessness in the city of Los Angeles. More specifically, in an interview given and
published on May 7, 2022, when asked about how she would address the homelessness
issue she responded, “There’s a big chunk of land in Palmdale and maybe we could
create a village out there.” Palmdale City Council immediately denounced then mayoral
candidate Bass’ comments and invited her to visit Palmdale to work collaboratively on
solutions before trying to export her city’s homeless to our community. She has yet to
accept our offer. Bass’ emergency order allows her to demand that departments identify
all city-owned properties that can be used for some form of housing. The City of Los
Angeles owns approximately 17,000 acres of bare land with few if any improvements in
and around the Plant 42 installation.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution Proclaiming a Local Emergency Regarding Homelessness
December 21, 2022
Page 2

DISCUSSION
There exists little to no infrastructure or services in place to effectively manage and assist
in addressing this crisis. The idea that Los Angeles could export homelessness problems
on Palmdale’s working class, family-oriented desert community on an emergency basis,
without allowing time for community and cross-agency communications is deeply
disturbing. Rather the City of Los Angeles should take the time to collaborate on
equitable, community-based solutions to address this humanitarian crisis.
A declaration of emergency would allow the City of Palmdale to activate an emergency
operations team in response to this proposal. It would allow Palmdale to have the tools
and resources necessary to mitigate the negative impacts of actions which are taken on
an emergency basis and which could permanently and negatively impact the safety of
persons and property within Palmdale. Granting such tools would encourage the City
of Los Angeles to work cooperatively with Palmdale, and all its neighboring jurisdictions
to create sustainable, rather than unnecessarily rushed and damaging short term
“solutions.”

FISCAL IMPACT
Unknown but estimated in the hundreds of thousands to manage costs associated with
dramatically increasing the local unhoused population to include social services,
emergency response teams, health and safety needs, media, etc.

  WHEREAS, the Los Angeles Times has reported that there are currently more than
42,000 people who are homeless in the City of Los Angeles;

  WHEREAS, the City of Los Angeles owns approximately 17,000 acres of bare land
with few if any improvements in and around Palmdale’s Plant 42 installation.

  WHEREAS, on May 7, 2022, Karen Bass, when asked about how she would
address the homelessness issue stated, “There’s a big chunk of land in Palmdale and
maybe we could create a village out there”;

  WHEREAS, on her first day of office, as the newly elected Mayor of Los Angeles,
Karen Bass declared a state of emergency relating to homelessness;

  WHEREAS, Government Code 8634 states in part, “During a local emergency the
governing body of a political subdivision, or officials designated thereby, may promulgate
orders and regulations necessary to provide for the protection of life and property,
including orders or regulations imposing a curfew within designated boundaries where
necessary to preserve the public order and safety. Such orders and regulations and
amendments and rescissions thereof shall be in writing and shall be given widespread
publicity and notice.”

  WHEREAS, it is currently unclear as to exactly what actions the City of Los
Angeles would take to attempt to resolve the homeless crisis, and whether, or to what
extent its emergency powers would be used to create a homeless “village”, and whether,
and to what extent such village would cause negative secondary effects which would
require immediate action to resolve;

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale supports taking well-reasoned and long-term
solutions to the ongoing issues relating to housing and homelessness, rather than short-
term solution which, when not properly planned, can cause multiple negative and
unplanned secondary impacts which can cause significant legal issues;

  WHEREAS, the Mayor of the City of Los Angeles declaring an emergency
establishes extreme peril to the safety of persons and property within Palmdale, and such
conditions are or are likely to be beyond the control of the services, personnel, equipment
and facilities of this City, requiring the combined forces of other political subdivisions to

  WHEREAS, the Palmdale City Manager serves as the City’s Director of
